channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Natural gas: Storage deficit and policy support – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey report that EU Natural gas storage has risen above 40% but remains well below the five-year average. With peace talks stalling and LNG disruptions from the Middle East, they see rising risks of tighter supply into winter.

item.title: Gold: Near-term pressure, longer-term strength – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists have cut their Gold forecasts for the next two quarters as higher inflation expectations from supply shocks lift yields and keep the Dollar firm, with markets even pricing a potential Fed hike in late 2026.

item.title: SNB’s Schlegel: We raise readiness to intervene against Swiss Franc’s appreciation
item.description: Swiss National Bank (SNB) Chairman Martin Schlegel said during the European trading session on Tuesday that the central bank is now more ready to intervene against one-way appreciating moves in the Swiss Franc (CHF).

item.title: Silver bounces back despite continued uncertainty over US-Iran peace deal
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades 1.85% higher to near $76.30 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The white metal gains as oil prices have corrected, while uncertainty surrounding the United States (US)-Iran remains intact.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ expectations clash with intervention risk – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage highlights a strong JGB auction and falling yields as markets price a 76% chance of a Bank of Japan (BoJ) rate hike this month. Despite this, USD/JPY remains near 160 for a fourth day, with Japanese officials issuing repeated intervention warnings.

item.title: Euro stalls below 1.1650 with all eyes on US JOLTS Job Openings
item.description: The Euro (EUR) appreciates higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, although the pair remains capped below 1.1650.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed data support firmer Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes that the May ISM manufacturing index points to a more restrictive Federal Reserve (Fed) stance and a firmer US Dollar (USD), with the headline index rising to a four-year high.

item.title: Euro area: Inflation keeps ECB on hiking path – Nordea
item.description: Nordea economists Tuuli Koivu and Anders Svendsen say rising Euro-area headline and core inflation, driven mainly by higher energy costs and robust services prices, strengthens the case for an ECB rate hike in June.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Consolidation before breakout against Euro – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts observe that EUR/PLN is trading near an ascending trendline from February 2025 and oscillating around its 200-day moving average. The pair is currently confined within a 4.2100–4.2650 consolidation band.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD recovery stalls below $4,540 amid cautious markets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) bounces up on Tuesday, retracing Monday's losses and returning to levels beyond $4,500.

item.title: ECB’s Rehn: Interest rate hike in June should be viewed as an insurance move
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) official and Finnish Central Bank Governor Olli Rehn said during the European trading session on Tuesday that an interest rate hike at the policy meeting this month should be viewed as an "insurance" move to guard against future inflation risks.

item.title: Euro consolidates losses against the British Pound despite high inflation figures
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains vulnerable against the British Pound (GBP) on Tuesday, capped below 0.8650, consolidating losses from the previous two trading days.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ cycle and consolidation against AUD – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists focus on AUD/NZD after a sharp post-RBNZ selloff. They argue the start of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) hiking cycle versus a peaking Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) cycle should cap the prior AUD/NZD uptrend, but expect short-term consolidation.

item.title: Euro: Neutral tone within defined band against dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann describe EUR/USD as neutral after Monday’s reversal from 1.1606 to close at 1.1630. They expect the pair to consolidate intraday between 1.1610 and 1.1660, while the broader 1.1590–1.1685 range remains in force.

item.title: Brent: Hormuz disruption sustains price pressure – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen highlights that Brent futures near the mid-$90s per barrel, down from a recent peak of $108, still reflect only a relatively optimistic scenario for the Iran conflict.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise near 160 with BoJ in focus – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Philip Wee highlights that USD/JPY is again trading near 160, keeping markets wary of potential Japanese authorities’ intervention and a possible 25 bps rate hike by the Bank of Japan (BoJ) to 1% at its June meeting.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $76.37 per troy ounce, up 2.00% from the $74.87 it cost on Monday.

item.title: Indian Rupee trades flat, US JOLTS Job Openings data in focus
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades almost flat against the US Dollar (USD) during India's afternoon trading hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Copper: Tariff decision risk supports prices – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that Copper prices in New York and London have risen ahead of a key US tariff decision. The Commerce Department is considering phased import duties starting at 15% in 2027, widening the US price premium and drawing more shipments to US ports.

item.title: Eurozone core inflation rises beyond expectations: Here's what it means for EUR/USD
item.description: Eurozone preliminary Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) data for May has come in at 3.2% year-on-year (YoY), as expected, higher than the April reading of 3%.

item.title: British Pound: Outlook shifts from bearish to neutral – OCBC
item.description: OCBC's strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong shift their British Pound (GBP) view from bearish to neutral, citing easing fiscal concerns and attractive carry that have helped GBP recover from early May losses.

item.title: US Dollar: Neutral near term, weaker over 2026 – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists keep a neutral near-term view on the US Dollar (USD) but maintains a bearish bias over the rest of 2026.

item.title: Gold bulls seem hesitant as Iran deal uncertainty and hawkish Fed bets counter softer USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) clings to modest intraday gains through the first half of the European session on Tuesday, though it lacks follow-through buying and remains below the previous day's swing high.

item.title: Polish Zloty: NBP seen on extended hold – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts expect the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to keep its policy rate unchanged at 3.75%, with a status quo stance likely through the second half of 2026 and early 2027. Inflation is currently within target, while growth has improved.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Sits near one-month high, below 160.00 intervention threshold
item.description: The USD/JPY pair extends its sideways consolidative price move through the first half of the European session on Tuesday and currently trades around the 159.70-159.75 region, or over a one-month top.

item.title: British Pound holds gains as US Dollar weakens on easing risk aversion
item.description: GBP/USD gains ground after registering minor losses in the previous day, trading around 1.3470 during the European hours on Tuesday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) loses ground on easing risk aversion due to a partial ceasefire between Hezbollah and Israel.

item.title: Oil: Price rebound drives FX shifts – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team notes that Brent crude briefly traded above USD 97 before easing below USD 95 as Iran–US ceasefire negotiations fluctuated. They highlight reports that OPEC+ may modestly lift July output, but see limited price impact unless exports rise.

item.title: Experts agree: Gold is going nowhere as long as Iran war continues
item.description: Gold is navigating a challenging environment as tight global energy markets and quickly shifting central bank expectations alter investor sentiment.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Kiwi hesitates around 0.5930 with risk appetite subdued
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is going through a nervous consolidation against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. The pair is looking for direction around 0.5930, following a reversal from 0.6000 on Monday, as investors remain wary of risk, awaiting developments in the Middle East conflict.

item.title: European Parliament moves to cut US tariffs, averting a trade clash
item.description: European Parliament's trade committee announces that it has voted in favor of legislation to remove European Union (EU) duties on many United States (US) goods imports.
